previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of moderate aortic stenosis, chronic hyponatremia due to SIADH, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted after being found to have a rapid ventricular rate during an outpatient cardiology visit, following a recent similar admission. He was asymptomatic from the tachycardia but had leukocytosis and a chest X-ray concerning for pneumonia, leading to treatment with vancomycin and cefepime for healthcare-associated pneumonia. Rate control was achieved using metoprolol succinate and digoxin, with stable sodium levels and no evidence of myocardial injury. Due to dysphagia, TEE-guided cardioversion was deferred, and anticoagulation with warfarin was initiated with plans for cardioversion in one month. Mild pulmonary edema was managed with furosemide, and recommendations were made to continue nighttime inhalers for chronic bronchitis. He was discharged to an extended care facility to complete one final dose of IV antibiotics, with follow-up appointments scheduled in cardiology and pain clinic.
